I was reading the Reddit lose it sub one day, and someone suggested logging food as an excellent way to track calories and lose weight. I decided to give it a go. And that's where my weight loss journey truly began. I bought a scale, and my weight was 193.2 lbs. Better than I had expected. I told myself this time to be positive, be kind to myself, just try my best, and aim for 1 lb weight loss a week. At the beginning I lost more than a pound a week because I was obese, but even weeks where I only lost 0.5 lbs, I never got discouraged and gave up, I just kept going. I started thinking of weight loss as a game, and had fun logging my food into Livestrong's MyPlate tracker. And as the weight kept steadily coming off with calorie counting, I realized that I could really do this this time around. I set goals for myself, and kept a weight loss journal. I wrote in it every weigh in day once a week. I wrote how excited I was that it was working, and every weight loss goal I achieved, I felt so proud of myself and would buy some clothes. My pants were falling off me, everything was loose and baggy. I could finally pick out cute clothes I actually liked and not just something that fit and would hide my body.

That weight loss journey began 3 years ago. Fast forward to today, and I am a very healthy 125lbs. I feel so good about myself, and I know I can maintain my weight for the rest of my life. I did it slow, never deprived myself, just ate less and was mindful. I realized that I will need to continue to log my food in, just because it helps keep me accountable, and it's just a part of my life at this point. I doesn't feel like a chore, and I know exactly what I need to do in order to maintain, so why would I throw that away? I've been maintaining a healthy weight for about 1.5 years now. You can't regain the weight back unless you start eating more than you're supposed to. It's all about balance.

TL;DR Was obese most of my life, lost the weight 3 years ago and have been maintaining a BMI of 22 ever since. You're in control of your weight, if you lose weight and then go back to eating too much, you will regain it. You won't just magically gain if you're eating the correct amount for your body, no matter if you were obese before or not.

It is true that we cannot lose fat cells. Science believes that the number of cells is set in childhood or early adolescence. Once they are there, they are there, and the only way to remove the cells is via liposuction. These cells do die off, but are replaced by new cells. I think the average life expectancy for a fat cell is 7 years.

However all this does NOT mean someone who is fat can't become thin, because our fat cells shrink and expand to accommodate our needs. It all goes back to our hunter/gatherer days when food was not guaranteed. If there was a good kill and that human ate more than his body required, the excess would be stored as fat. If food was scarce and that human had to go a while without eating (or was only eating very little) the fat on his body would provide energy for daily functioning.

We haven't evolved a whole lot since then. Our bodies still do the same thing; they will store fat if we eat more than we need, and they will burn fat if we eat less than we need. You will often see this referred to as CICO - Calories In, Calories Out. Calories In are the calories you eat & drink, and Calories Out are the calories you expend doing daily things such as walking, breathing, digesting, etc. Simply put, CICO is like an equation: if Calories In > Calories Out, you will gain weight. If Calories In = Calories Out, you will stay the same weight. If Calories In < Calories Out, you will lose weight.

However, our environment has changed since prehistoric times. Foods that are high in calories are readily available everywhere you look. These junk foods are typically high in salt, fat, and sugar, or all three. They provide little, if any, nutritional value, but they still add to your caloric intake (sugar is especially bad for this). That's why these types of foods are often called "empty calories" - they count as calories, but they do not provide your body with any nutrients. They are also not very filling. Many people consume too many of these types of foods and gain weight. However, consuming too much of any food will make you gain weight - even veggies!

So what does this all have to do with diet and weight loss? Everything! Weight loss is achieved when you eat fewer calories than you burn (Calories In < Calories Out). But how many calories do you burn in a day? This number is referred to as your TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) which you can calculate easily online - tdeecalculator.net is the one I use. Once you have your TDEE, you need to eat below that number to lose weight. But how do you know how many calories are in your food? Again, you can use a calculator or online food journal. I like MyFitnessPal because it's free and easy to use. It will even calculate your TDEE and set your goals. But to get accurate calorie counts, you have to weigh and measure your food. 100g of strawberries will have twice as many calories as 50g of strawberries, and humans are really bad at guessing how much something weighs or how many calories it has just by looking at it.

Long-term weight loss IS possible. The "95% of diets fail" was taken from a study in 1957 I believe with fewer than 50 subjects. So the results aren't really that reliable. However, many people go on a "diet" that is not sustainable - it's either too hard to follow, doesn't provide adequate nutrition, is too expensive (like those shakes you buy online) or whatever. Also, many people think that going on a diet is a quick fix - that you can do the diet for a certain length of time, lose some weight, and go back to the way things were before without gaining the weight back. That is simply not true. In order for weight loss to be effective and permanent, you need to change your lifestyle. For example, if a person ate nothing except take-out pizzas before going on a diet, then lost weight by eating nothing but veggies and lean meats on a diet, and then resumed eating nothing but pizzas, the weight will come back. You need to adopt healthy eating and exercise habits for the weight loss to stick. You need to hold yourself accountable, be honest when you are counting calories, and be disciplined enough to continue eating well and exercising even after you have lost the weight.

TL;DR: Weight loss is achieved through lifestyle changes, not a quick-fix diet
